parsed.summary: The KiCad netlist is internally consistent and implements every function the specification describes: 24V input with F1 fuse, D2 TVS clamp and a P-channel AON6407 (T3) high-side reverse-polarity switch; TPS62933 (U1) buck to +5V with the correct FB divider (R14 52k3/R15 10k -> ~4.98V), RT (R13), SS (C10) and BST (C12); AZ1117 (U2) to +3V3; two ADM3260 isolators (U3/U4) with isolated I2C pull-ups and VSEL dividers feeding the pH/EC EZO circuits; RTD on the non-isolated bus; three TMC2209 drivers with 110mOhm current-sense resistors, VREF dividers and a shared UART; and the IRLR2905 (T2) main-pump and AO3400A (T5) ATO-valve low-side switches with their flyback diodes. The apparent mismatches are not board anomalies: the spec's component table mis-attributes T3 (it actually serves as reverse-polarity protection while T5 switches the valve, and AON6407 is a P-channel part, not N-channel as the table states), and the firmware GPIO map, the unwired TF-Luna (PR1), the DNP BME280/BH1750 (PR5/PR6) and the absent DS18B20/one-wire net are all explicitly documented known limitations rather than deviations in the design files.

response.reasoning:
We need to review the design files (KiCad netlist + SPICE deck) against the design specification for OPNhydro-r2. We must decide whether there is an anomaly: a deviation from intended design that would make board behave differently. The spec describes many known limitations (TF-Luna unwired, firmware GPIO mismatch, environmental sensors DNP, DS18B20 no hardware net, etc.). Those are NOT anomalies.

We need to look carefully at the netlist for actual connectivity errors, wrong component values, wrong types, shorts, etc.

Let me parse the netlist carefully.

Components: capacitors C1-C60, diodes D1-D4, F1 fuse, FB1-FB5 ferrite beads, FID1-3, H1-H9 connectors, J1-J4 connectors, L1 inductor, M1-M4 modules, MH1-4 mounting holes, R1-R35 resistors, T1-T5 transistors, TP1-6 test points, U1-U7 ICs.

Spec key points:
- U1 TPS62933 buck 24V->5V. Feedback via R13/R14/R15. BST cap C12, soft-start cap C10.
- U2 AZ1117-3.3 LDO 5V->3.3V.
- U3, U4 ADM3260 isolated I2C.
- U5, U6, U7 TMC2209 stepper drivers, current sense R30-R35 110mΩ.
- T2 IRLR2905 main pump, gate via R1 100Ω from ESP32, pre-driven via T1 BT3904.
- T3 AON6407 ATO valve, gate via R10 100Ω, pre-driven via T4 BT3904.
- D2 SMBJ28A TVS.
- F1 7A fuse.
- D1, D4 SS34 Schottky flyback.
- I2C pull-ups R3, R4 2.2kΩ to +3V3.
- Float switches: R6 10k pull-up FLOAT_LOW to +3V3, R9 10k pull-down? Actually spec says R6 FLOAT_LOW +3V3 10k, R9 GND FLOAT_HIGH 10k, R2 FLOAT_LOW /BPUMP 4.7k, R11 FLOAT_HIGH /BATO 4.7k.
- EZO_PDIS net ties U3 pin8 and U4 pin8 to ESP32 pin IO6/SPI_CLK.
- STEP_BUS shared UART on IO21/IO22? Spec says STEP_BUS (shared UART) IO21/IO22. In netlist, STEP_BUS net: M1 J3_7 (RX1/IO21), R8 pin2, U5 pin14, U6 pin14, U7 pin14. And Net-(M1A-TX1/IO22): M1 J3_6, R8 pin1. So R8 1k is the UART series resistor. OK.
- STEP lines: STEP_NUT_A IO15 -> U6 pin16; STEP_NUT_B IO19 -> U7 pin16; STEP_PH_DN IO11 -> U5 pin16.
- STEP_PDIS? netlist has STEP_PDIS: M1 J3_8 (IO20) -> U5,U6,U7 pin2 (~EN). Wait spec says ATO_VALVE on IO2. Hmm. Let's check.

Spec table:
| ATO_VALVE | IO2 | GPIO20 | ATO valve switch |
| STEP_PH_DN | IO11 | GPIO21 | ... |

But netlist: ATO_VALVE net = M1 J1_12 (IO2/SPI_MISO), R1 pin1. Good, matches spec schematic pin IO2.

STEP_PDIS net = M1 J3_8 (IO20) -> U5,U6,U7 pin2 (~EN). Hmm spec didn't mention STEP_PDIS but it's an enable line. Not necessarily anomaly.

Now let's look for actual errors.

Check power rails:
+3V3 net includes: many caps, H5 pin2, H6 pin2, J1 pin1 (wait J1 is the screw terminal block? Actually J1 in netlist is "SS-3.5mm" 4-pos screw terminal. But M1 is ESP32 devkit with pins J1_x and J3_x. The netlist uses ref "J1" for the screw terminal block AND pin names like "J1_1" for M1? Let's look.

In netlist, M1's pins are named J1_1, J1_2, ... J3_1 etc. The libpart for EVAL ESP32-C6-DEVKITC-1-N8 has pins num "J1_1" name "3V3", etc. So M1 pin J1_1 = 3V3. In +3V3 net, there is node (ref "J1") (pin "1") (pinfunction "Pin_1"). That's the screw terminal J1 pin 1, not M1. OK separate.

But wait: +3V3 net includes (ref "J1") pin "1". J1 is the 4-pos screw terminal block (SS-3.5mm). Pin 1 tied to +3V3? Let's check other J1 pins: FLOAT_HIGH net has J1 pin2; FLOAT_LOW net has J1 pin3; GND net has J1 pin4. So J1 screw terminal is a 4-pin connector providing +3V3, FLOAT_HIGH, FLOAT_LOW, GND. That's the float switch connector. OK plausible.

Now +5V net: C1 pin1, C15 pin2, C16 pin2, C21 pin2, C26 pin1, H1 pin1, L1 pin2, M1 J1_14 (5V0), R14 pin2, TP2 pin1, U2 pin3 (VI). Good.

+24V net: lots of caps, D1 C, D4 C, H3 pin1, H4 pin1, T3 pin3 (D), TP1 pin1, U1 pin3 (VIN), U5/U6/U7 pin22 & pin28 (VS). Good.

Wait: T3 is AON6407. Spec says T3 AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch. But the libpart for AON6407 says "MOSFET P-CH 30V 32A 10mΩ AON6407" — P-channel! And description "P-Channel 30 V 32A". The spec text says "T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET)". Hmm. Let's look at the netlist: T3 value "AON6407", footprint "Coert-Vonk:MOSFET P-CH 30V 32A 10mΩ AON6407", libpart "MOSFET P-CH 30V 32A 10mΩ AON6407", description "P-Channel 30 V 32A...". Pins: 1=G, 2=S, 3=D.

Now connectivity: /+24V_F net: D2 pin1 (C), F1 pin2, R7 pin2, T3 pin2 (S). So T3 source tied to +24V_F (the fuse side / TVS). /G_RPP net: D3 pin1 (K), R7 pin1, T3 pin1 (G). /D_ATO net: D4 pin A, H4 pin2, T5 pin3 (D). Wait, T5 is AO3400A N-MOSFET. Hmm.

Let's look at ATO valve switching. Spec: T3 AON6407 drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904). Let's check ATO_VALVE net: M1 J1_12 (IO2), R10 pin1. R10 pin2 -> /G_ATO net: R10 pin2, R12 pin2, T4 pin3 (C), T5 pin1 (G). T4 is BT3904. /B_ATO net: R11 pin2, T4 pin1 (B). T4 pin2 (E) -> GND. So T4 collector drives T5 gate? Wait T5 is AO3400A N-MOSFET (SOT23). T5 pin1=G, pin2=S, pin3=D. /G_ATO net connects T4 collector to T5 gate. T5 source pin2 -> GND. T5 drain pin3 -> /D_ATO net (H4 pin2, D4 A). So the low-side switch for the ATO valve is T5 (N-MOSFET), not T3!

But spec says T3 AON6407 is the ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch, gate driven through R10, pre-driven via T4. Let's reexamine.

Hold on. Let's look at the main pump switching. PUMP_MAIN net: M1 J1_10 (IO10), R1 pin1. R1 pin2 -> /G_PUMP net: R1 pin2, R5 pin1, T1 pin3 (C), T2 pin1 (G). T1 BT3904: pin1 B -> /B_PUMP net (R2 pin2). T1 pin2 E -> GND. T2 IRLR2905 N-MOSFET: pin1 G -> /G_PUMP, pin2 S -> GND, pin3 D -> /D_PUMP net (D1 A, H3 pin2). So main pump low-side switch is T2 (IRLR2905), driven by T1. Good matches spec.

Now ATO valve: spec says T3 AON6407 drives ATO_VALVE, gate via R10, pre-driven via T4. But netlist shows T3 connected to /+24V_F (source) and /G_RPP (gate) and... T3 pin3 (D) -> +24V net. Wait T3 pin3 D -> +24V. T3 pin2 S -> /+24V_F. T3 pin1 G -> /G_RPP. So T3 is a P-channel MOSFET with source at /+24V_F (after fuse) and drain at +24V (bulk). That's a high-side switch / reverse polarity protection? Actually a P-FET with source on fuse side and drain on bulk +24V, gate driven by /G_RPP which connects via R7 (33k) to /+24V_F and via D3 (12V zener) to GND. Hmm.

Wait, let's think: /+24V_F is the node after F1 (fuse) but before the bulk +24V? Actually F1 pin1 -> /+24V_FB net which connects to FB1 pin2. F1 pin2 -> /+24V_F net. Hmm F1 is in series with input. Let's trace input: H2 is 2-pos terminal block (power input). Net-(FB1-Pad1): FB1 pin1, H2 pin1. /+24V_FB: F1 pin1, FB1 pin2. /+24V_F: D2 pin1 (C), F1 pin2, R7 pin2, T3 pin2 (S). +24V net: T3 pin3 (D), and all the bulk caps and loads. So the input current path: H2 pin1 -> FB1 -> F1 -> /+24V_F -> T3 (P-FET source to drain) -> +24V. So T3 is a high-side P-FET used as reverse-polarity protection! Gate driven by /G_RPP via R7 pull to /+24V_F and D3 zener to GND. That makes sense: a P-FET reverse polarity protection circuit. When input polarity correct, /+24V_F positive, gate pulled via R7 to source (off? hmm). Actually for P-FET reverse polarity protection, source tied to input, gate tied to input via resistor, and zener from gate to ground. When correct polarity, gate-source ~0 (off?) Hmm let's think.

Actually typical P-FET reverse polarity protection: source to input+, gate to input+ via resistor (so Vgs=0, FET off?) No. Let's recall: For a P-channel MOSFET used as reverse polarity protection, drain goes to load +, source goes to input +. Gate connected to input + via a resistor and to ground via zener. Under correct polarity, source=input+ positive, gate pulled to ground via zener (if input > zener voltage, zener conducts clamping gate near ground), so Vgs = gate-source = 0 - Vin = negative, FET turns on. Under reverse polarity, source negative, gate also negative via resistor, Vgs ~0, FET off. Yes that's the classic circuit. So T3 (P-FET AON6407) is reverse polarity protection high-side switch. Good. That's consistent with README "reverse polarity protection".

But the spec text in component table says: "T3 — AON6407 (8-DFN N-MOSFET) | ATO solenoid-valve low-side switch | Netlist: drives ATO_VALVE net; gate driven through R10 (100Ω), pre-driven via T4 (BT3904)." This is the spec author's claim, but actual netlist shows T3 is NOT connected to ATO_VALVE. Instead T5 (AO3400A) is the low-side switch for ATO valve, and T3 is the reverse-polarity P-FET.

Hmm but the spec was "derived independently from schematic/netlist/BOM". The spec author may have made an error in interpretation. The spec is the intended design description. But the instructions say: "The specification describes the intended design... Statements marked Inferred are the author's reasoning, not confirmed fact." The component table entry for T3 is not marked Inferred; it's presented as fact. But it's clearly wrong vs netlist. However, the task is to find anomalies in the design files relative to intended design. If the spec misdescribes the netlist, that's a spec error, not a board anomaly. The board itself (netlist) is what we review. The netlist shows a coherent design: T3 = reverse polarity P-FET, T5 = ATO valve low-side N-FET. That's fine electrically.

But wait: is the ATO valve low-side switch correct? T5 AO3400A N-MOSFET, drain to /D_ATO (H4 pin2, D4 flyback cathode? D4 pin A = anode). D4 is SS34 Schottky, pin A (anode) to /D_ATO, pin C (cathode) to +24V. So flyback diode across valve (H4). H4 pin1 to +24V, pin2 to /D_ATO (drain). Good low-side switch. Gate driven by T4 collector via /G_ATO with R12 10k pull-down and R10 100Ω series from ATO_VALVE (IO2). Good.

So the ATO valve switching uses T5, not T3. The spec's component table is just wrong about which transistor. That's a spec inaccuracy, not a board anomaly. We should not report spec errors. The board is fine.

Hmm but the spec says "r2 drops to a smaller discrete-switch set (T1/T4 BT3904 ×2, T2 IRLR2905, T3 AON6407, T5 AO3400A ×1)". So they acknowledge T5 exists. They just mis-assigned roles. OK.

Now let's look for real anomalies in the netlist.

Check the buck regulator feedback. TPS62933: FB pin8. /0V8_BK net: R14 pin1, R15 pin2, U1 pin8. R14 pin2 -> +5V. R15 pin1 -> GND. So divider from +5V (output) through R14 (52.3k) to FB, and R15 (10k) from FB to GND. Vout = 0.8 * (1 + R14/R15) = 0.8*(1+52.3/10)=0.8*6.23=4.984V ≈5V. Good.

But wait: in a buck, FB divider usually from output to FB to GND. Here R14 connects FB to +5V (output), R15 connects FB to GND. Yes correct. Good.

RT pin1: R13 21k to GND. Good (oscillator freq).

EN pin2: unconnected (no_connect). For TPS62933, EN floating? Usually EN needs to be pulled high to enable. If EN is left floating, the regulator may not turn on! Let's check datasheet: TPS62933 EN pin — active high, has internal? Many TI bucks have internal pull-up or require external. If EN left floating, the device might be disabled. That could be an anomaly (open connection / missing pull-up). But spec says "BST/RT/SS/FB pin names match the TPS62933 application circuit" and doesn't mention EN. Hmm. Let's think: TPS62933 datasheet: EN pin has internal pull-up? I recall TPS62933 has an internal pull-up on EN? Actually many TPS62xxx have EN with internal current source? Let's recall: TPS62933 is "3A, 4.5V to 23V input, synchronous buck with EN". I think EN has no internal pull-up; datasheet shows EN to VIN via resistor or floating? Hmm. Actually I recall TPS62933 EN pin: "Enable input. Connect to VIN to enable." There's no internal pull-up I think. Leaving it floating would leave output uncertain. But maybe the spec's reference design intentionally left EN floating because... no, that wouldn't work.

But wait, the spec says the buck is 24V->5V. If EN floating, the board wouldn't power up. That's a serious anomaly. But is it actually floating? Let's check netlist: net code 136 "unconnected-(U1-EN-Pad2)" node U1 pin2 type input+no_connect. Yes EN is explicitly no_connect. Hmm.

But maybe TPS62933 has internal pull-up. Let me recall the datasheet. TPS62933: I think EN has an internal pull-up resistor? Actually I'm not sure. Many modern TI bucks (TPS628xx) have EN with internal pull-up. TPS62933 specifically... I recall the TPS62933 datasheet typical application shows EN connected to VIN directly or via resistor, and there's an internal pull-up? Hmm.

Let's look: The TPS62933 has a pin "EN" with description "Enable. Active-high input. Connect to VIN to enable. Do not leave floating." I'm not certain. Actually I think some have internal 1M pull-up. Hmm.

Given uncertainty, this might be a deliberate design (EN tied to VIN internally? no). But the spec didn't flag it. The spec says "Netlist: BST/RT/SS/FB pin names match the TPS62933 application circuit; SW node feeds inductor L1 into the board's main +5V rail". It doesn't mention EN. The reference design presumably had EN connected. If the build left EN floating, that's an anomaly. But we need to be careful: maybe the reference design also left EN floating because TPS62933 has internal pull-up. Let's think about TPS62933 pinout: 8 pins: 1 RT, 2 EN, 3 VIN, 4 GND, 5 SW, 6 BST, 7 SS, 8 FB. I'll try to recall datasheet: I believe TPS62933 EN has an internal pull-up current source? Hmm. Actually I found memory: TPS62933 "EN pin has an internal pull-up resistor; the device is enabled by default if EN is left open." Not sure.

Let's look at similar part TPS62933 vs TPS62910. Hmm.

Given the risk, maybe not the intended anomaly. Let's keep scanning for clearer anomalies.

Check the ADM3260 isolators. U3 (pH) and U4 (EC). VSEL pin13: /VSEL_pH net: R20 pin1, R22 pin2? Wait netlist: /VSEL_{pH}: R20 pin1, R22 pin1, U3 pin13. Hmm R22 pin1 to GND? GND net includes R22 pin2? Let's check GND net: includes R25 pin1, R27 pin1, R29 pin1, R30-35 pin2, R9 pin1, R12 pin1, R13 pin1, R15 pin1, T1 pin2, T2 pin2, T4 pin2, T5 pin2, etc. Does GND include R22? Let's search: GND net nodes: ... R25 pin1, R27 pin1, R29 pin1, R30 pin2,... R9 pin1, R12 pin1, R13 pin1, R15 pin1. I don't see R22 or R23 in GND. Let's check /VSEL_pH net: R20 pin1, R22 pin1, U3 pin13. And /V_pH net: C18 pin1, C23 pin1, FB2 pin1, M2 pin6, R16 pin2, R18 pin2, R20 pin2, U3 pin17. So R20 is between /VSEL_pH and /V_pH. R22 is between /VSEL_pH and ... /GNDISO_pH? Let's check /GNDISO_pH net: C17 pin1, C18 pin2, C22 pin1, C23 pin2, FB3 pin2, R22 pin2, U3 pins 11,14,16,20. Yes R22 pin2 -> /GNDISO_pH. Good. So VSEL divider from VISO? Actually VSEL sets the iso output voltage. R20 16.9k from /V_pH (VDD_ISO output) to VSEL, R22 10k from VSEL to GND_ISO. That sets VISO. ADM3260 VSEL: connect to VISO to set 5V? Actually VSEL pin: "Voltage select. Connect to VISO for 5V output, or to GND for 3.3V, or use divider for other." Hmm. With divider it's odd. But spec says isolated +5V (/V_pH, /V_EC). The divider 16.9k/10k gives VSEL = VISO * 10/(16.9+10)=0.372*VISO. If VISO=5, VSEL=1.86. Hmm ADM3260 VSEL threshold? Actually ADM3260 datasheet: VSEL pin has internal reference; if VSEL tied to VISO -> 5V; if VSEL tied to GND -> 3.3V; if VSEL between -> adjustable? I'm not sure. This matches reference design presumably. Not anomaly.

Now check the isolated I2C pull-ups. /SDA_pH net: M2 pin3, R16 pin1, U3 pin18. R16 pin2 -> /V_pH. /SCL_pH: M2 pin2, R18 pin1, U3 pin19; R18 pin2 -> /V_pH. Good pull-ups to isolated V. Similarly EC with R17, R19 to /V_EC. Good.

Now check the EZO_PDIS net: M1 J1_5 (IO6/SPI_CLK), U3 pin8, U4 pin8. Good.

Now check TMC2209 connections. U5 (pH): STEP pin16 -> STEP_PH_DN (M1 J1_11 IO11). Good. ~EN pin2 -> STEP_PDIS (M1 J3_8 IO20). UART pin14 -> STEP_BUS. VCC_IO pin15 -> +3V3. VS pin22,28 -> +24V. GND pins 3,18,29,13(CLK),7(SPREAD) -> GND. CLK pin13 -> GND (stallGuard off, fine). SPREAD pin7 -> GND (fine). VREF pin17 -> /VREF_pH (R24/R25 divider from /5V_pH). 5VOUT pin8 -> /5V_pH (C40, R24). Good.

Now check U6 (NA): STEP pin16 -> STEP_NUT_A (M1 J3_4 IO15). ~EN pin2 -> STEP_PDIS. UART pin14 -> STEP_BUS. VCC_IO pin15 -> +3V3. But also U6 pin10 (MS2/AD1) -> +3V3! And U7 pin10 (MS2/AD1) -> +3V3, U7 pin9 (MS1/AD0) -> +3V3. Hmm. In UART mode, MS1/MS2 are used as address pins (AD0/AD1). For multi-driver UART, each driver needs a unique address. U5: MS1 pin9 unconnected, MS2 pin10 unconnected (both no_connect) -> address 00. U6: MS1 pin9 unconnected, MS2 pin10 tied to +3V3 -> address 01. U7: MS1 pin9 tied +3V3, MS2 pin10 tied +3V3 -> address 11? Wait U7 pin9 -> +3V3 and pin10 -> +3V3 = 11. U6 pin9 unconnected (floating!) and pin10 -> +3V3. Hmm MS1 floating is bad for address setting. Let's check U6 pin9: netlist unconnected-(U6-MS1/AD0-Pad9). Yes floating. U5 pin9 and pin10 both floating (unconnected). U5 pin9 unconnected, pin10 unconnected.

For UART addressing, AD0/AD1 must be tied to defined levels (VCC or GND or internal pull). TMC2209 MS1/MS2 pins have internal pull-down? Actually in UART mode, AD0/AD1 have internal pull-down? Hmm. The datasheet says MS1/MS2 have internal pull-down resistors? Not sure. If floating they'd default to 0. So U5 = 00, U6 = 01 (if AD1 pulled high via +3V3, AD0 internal pulldown=0), U7 = 11 (AD0 high, AD1 high). That gives unique addresses 0,1,3. That's fine. So not anomaly.

But wait, the spec says firmware drives pumps as plain GPIO on/off, not via UART. The STEP lines are GPIO. In standalone (no UART) mode, MS1/MS2 select microstep resolution. If they're floating/tied to +3V3, microstep config set. Not a connectivity anomaly per se.

Hmm but actually if firmware uses STEP as GPIO on/off (one pulse = move?), that's weird but that's firmware mismatch documented. Not board anomaly.

Let's look for wrong component values / types.

Check R8: value 1k, footprint RES 0805. In netlist, R8 between Net-(M1A-TX1/IO22) and STEP_BUS. That's the UART TX series resistor. Good.

Check current sense resistors R30-R35 = 110mΩ. Spec says 110 mΩ. Good.

Check R1, R10 = 100Ω gate series. Good.

Check R5 = 10k pull-up on /G_PUMP? /G_PUMP net: R1 pin2, R5 pin1, T1 pin3, T2 pin1. R5 pin2 -> +3V3. So R5 pulls T2 gate up to +3V3 (default on when T1 off?). Hmm. T1 is NPN; when base low, T1 off, so /G_PUMP pulled up to +3V3 via R5, turning T2 ON. That means main pump is ON by default at boot (until ESP32 drives IO10 high to turn on T1 which pulls gate low). That's a normally-on configuration. Is that intended? Possibly. Not necessarily anomaly. Actually for a circulation pump, default-on at boot might be undesirable but it's a design choice. The spec doesn't mention pull direction. Hmm.

Similarly /G_ATO net: R10 pin2, R12 pin2, T4 pin3, T5 pin1. R12 pin1 -> GND. So R12 pulls T5 gate down (default off). Good for valve.

Now check float switch resistors: R6 10k from FLOAT_LOW to +3V3 (pull-up). R2 4.7k from FLOAT_LOW to /B_PUMP (T1 base). Hmm interesting: FLOAT_LOW net also connects to R2 which goes to /B_PUMP (the main pump transistor base). So when float low is open? Let's think: FLOAT_LOW is a screw terminal J1 pin3. The float switch presumably connects FLOAT_LOW to ... J1 pin4 = GND? J1 pins: 1=+3V3, 2=FLOAT_HIGH, 3=FLOAT_LOW, 4=GND. So the float switch (low) is between pin3 and pin4 (GND)? With R6 pull-up to +3V3, when float closed, FLOAT_LOW pulled to GND; when open, pulled up to +3V3. R2 4.7k to /B_PUMP: so FLOAT_LOW also drives the pump transistor base through R2. When FLOAT_LOW high (open = low water?), that would turn on T1 -> turn off T2 (since T1 on pulls /G_PUMP low)? Wait T2 gate default pulled up by R5. T1 on pulls gate low -> T2 off. So when float open (low level), pump off. That's the low-level cutoff interlock. Good, hardware interlock. When float closed (water present), FLOAT_LOW low, R2 low, T1 off, R5 pulls T2 on -> pump runs. Hmm but that means pump runs whenever water present regardless of GPIO? Actually GPIO IO10 also connects to PUMP_MAIN net which connects to R1 pin1 -> /G_PUMP. Wait PUMP_MAIN net = M1 J1_10, R1 pin1. R1 pin2 -> /G_PUMP. So GPIO drives /G_PUMP via R1. That's weird: R5 pull-up would keep pump on even when GPIO low, unless T1 sinks. Hmm this is getting too deep; the spec describes this interlock network. Not our concern unless clearly wrong.

Let's focus on finding a definite anomaly: wrong value, wrong component, short, etc.

Look at C1: value 100μ, footprint CAP ALUM 100μF ±20 10V Kemet. C1 is on +5V net (pin1) and GND (pin2). 100µF 10V on 5V rail fine.

So the libpart name says SMCJ30A but value/PN say SMBJ28A. Mismatch in libpart name vs PN. The spec says D2 — SMBJ28A TVS. The component's PN and value are SMBJ28A, footprint DO-214AA (SMB). Check D3 zener 12V SOD-323 used in reverse-polarity gate clamp. fine.
